title: Ash Reshteh
subtitle: herb and noodle soup
excerpt: Ash Reshteh is a thick Persian soup packed with herbs, spinach and three kinds of legumes. It is finished with fried onions and a swirl of yoghurt. Serves 6.
sourceNotes: Ash Reshteh is one of the oldest Persian soups, traditionally made at Nowruz and during Ramadan. The noodles symbolise the threads of fate.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze without the yoghurt topping for up to 3 months. Add the yoghurt fresh when serving.

glossaryTerms.definition: The Persian term for thick, hearty soups that are substantial enough to serve as a meal on their own.
Flat noodles used in Persian cooking, symbolising the threads of fate and good fortune in the new year.

content.text: is a thick, filling soup made with herbs, spinach and three kinds of legumes. It uses flat
noodles in the traditional version; this recipe uses lentils as a thickener in their place. Serves 6.
The fried onion topping is not optional. Crispy, dark onions spooned over the soup at the table are what make it Persian rather than merely a vegetable broth.

items.prepNote: 2 finely diced, 1 thinly sliced for topping

content.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in the stockpot over medium heat. Fry the diced onions for 12 minutes until golden. Add the turmeric and stir for 1 minute.
Add the green lentils and water to the pot. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer and cook for 20 minutes until the lentils are just tender.

Add the kidney beans, chickpeas and haricot beans. Stir in the spinach, parsley and fenugreek leaves. The pot will look very full. Continue simmering for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the greens have wilted and the soup has thickened.
While the soup cooks, heat the remaining 2 tablespoons of oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the sliced onion for 18 to 20 minutes until very dark and crispy. These are the topping.
Taste the soup and adjust seasoning. Ladle into bowls and top each one with fried onions and a spoonful of plain yoghurt. Add crumbled dried chilli if using.

attrs.solution: Continue simmering uncovered for 10 to 15 minutes. The lentils will break down and the herbs will release starch to thicken the broth naturally.

attrs.problem: Fried onion topping burnt too quickly
attrs.solution: Lower the heat. Onions for topping need medium rather than high heat and patient stirring. They should be mahogany coloured, not black.
The fenugreek leaves give ash reshteh its distinctive slightly bitter note. If using dried fenugreek, increase the quantity by a third. Add a squeeze of lemon juice to brighten the flavour.

content.text: Ash Reshteh is eaten across Iran at Nowruz, the Persian New Year in March. It also appears during the last Wednesday of the Persian year. The noodles are said to represent the threads of fate. Eating them is thought to bring good luck for the year ahead. Some families cook a pot of this soup every time someone leaves on a long journey.
